messages:
Aisha Khan: Quick policy Q 1 1 1 - I9m relocating from US -> UK with an official move date of 2024-12-28. I had 2 full PTO days approved for 12/30-12/31 but HR cancelled them because of the company year-end blackout. My balance shows those 2 days dropped due to carryover cap. Since I was physically moving countries and not taking time off by choice, can we either convert them to floating holidays or carry them into 2025?
Priya (People Ops): Thanks for flagging this, Aisha. Relocation around the year-end can be messy because our blackout is applied based on your country of record on 12/31 (per policy) and payroll cutoff. Two paths: 1) Exception to carryover if the time off was pre-approved and move/relocation interfered; 2) Convert to 2 floating holidays (subject to manager sign-off). We'll need relocation docs and the original PTO approvals attached to a ticket.
Jon Mercer: I approved the 12/30-12/31 PTO. Aisha9s move was announced to the team on 2024-12-10 and we had coverage. I9m fine with either carryover or floating holiday conversion, whichever is simpler. :+1:
hr-bot: FYI: Year-end blackout policy: company-wide shutdown applies 12/24-12/31 inclusive for US-headquartered contracts. Local country holiday exceptions evaluated case-by-case. Payroll cutoff: 2024-12-31 23:59 UTC. See https://intranet.redwood/people/holiday-policy for details.
Priya (People Ops): Important note: because your country-of-record switches to UK on 12/28, payroll may consider you UK-based for pro-ration. That sometimes affects carryover caps and floating holiday availability. Please attach any relocation confirmation (visa, relocation stipend email, or move-in lease) so we can document the change date.
Aisha Khan: I9ll attach the relocation confirmation and the calendar approvals. One preference: can they be split into two half-days in Jan? I9d like one morning for admin and one afternoon for bank/UK GP setup.
Priya (People Ops): If we convert to floating holidays, you can absolutely use them as 0.5-day entries. If we get a carryover exception, Payroll will normally keep them as full days but we can request split usage on a case basis. Note: manager must approve each partial-day booking.
hr-bot: Reminder: Exception requests after payroll cutoff require escalation and may take 5-7 business days. Tickets created before cutoff have higher chance of in-cycle adjustment.
Aisha Khan: Ticket created: HR-2025-1123 (https://hr.redwood/tickets/HR-2025-1123). Attached: PTO approval screenshot, relocation confirmation email (12/10), and my manager note.
Priya (People Ops): Got it. Routing to Payroll + Global Mobility now. Tentative ETA 4 business days. If Payroll approves conversion to floating holidays we will post the change and update your PTO ledger. If they prefer carryover we will create the exception and note location change effective 2024-12-28.
Jon Mercer: Thx Priya. I9m fine with floating holidays. If Payroll needs a manager nod I9ll reply in the ticket.
Priya (People Ops): One more detail: if Payroll denies the exception because of local statutory restrictions, People Ops can offer a discretionary one-time ad-hoc floating day grant for relocation cases. We9ve used that in a few prior international transfers. Documented in the ticket history.
Aisha Khan: Amazing, appreciate the flexibility. I logged tentative 0.5-day entries in the PTO calendar for Jan 10 and Jan 14 so the team knows coverage needs.
hr-bot: Ticket HR-2025-1123 received. Estimated response time: 4 business days. For urgent processing, mark the ticket high priority and include manager confirmation.
Priya (People Ops): Will follow up here with the Payroll decision. If anyone else has had similar relocation/carryover experiences pls chime in with the ticket reference so we can streamline approvals.
